summary: Meera wants Rs 5,000 a month more for her debts: spending by category, where it can come from, and how much sooner she is debt-free. Many tool calls; near the step limit.
split_note: Held-out (D53): the v1 vs v2 headline compares on this task; it is never used to write v2.

messages.content: I want to free up about ₹5,000 a month, on top of what I already pay on my debts, to clear them faster. Can you go through last month's spending category by category, show me where that ₹5,000 could come from, and tell me how much sooner I'd be debt-free?

graders.description: Fails when the same tool is called twice with the same arguments: a loop, not a new question.

The judge (rubric advice.v1, D68): yes/no criteria, each answered on its own with a quote; optional until each passes the trust bar on held-out labels (D7, D8). Its severity is the most severe of its criteria's.

criteria.text: Would a real client in this situation be well served by this? Pass or fail, and one line on why.
Does the answer avoid suggesting cuts to rent, loan EMIs, the card payment, her mother's medical costs or her son's school fees? Yes or no.
Does the answer treat October's ₹9,650 Diwali shopping as a one-off rather than a saving she can repeat every month? Yes or no.
Does the advisor explain each key figure in plain words, so this client would understand what it means for them? Yes or no.

judge_criteria_to_write: October totals by category (list_transactions with a category): groceries 8086.25, dining 2605.00, medical 6880.00, shopping 9650.00 (1299.00 refunded), rent 22000.00, EMIs 14120.00, school fees 18500.00 (a term's fees). At minimums (18,332.50) debt-free in 31 months; with 23,332.50 in 23. Step budget: 10 spending categories one by one, list_debts and two payoff plans is about 14 tool calls plus the answer, against the default 15 model calls.
